leads.name: The Cork Oak of Pedragosa

location.address: Pedragosa, UF de Bensafrim e Barão de São João, Lagos municipality

leads.reason: Fully verified and written (story, recognition line, girth 350cm, ICNF public-interest designation 2011), then held rather than published on two grounds. First, one tree is well below the four-tree floor, and it does not clear the single-famous-tree exception either: nothing found (one regional blog roundup aside) establishes it as a tree people specifically travel for, unlike the Angel Oak or Castagno dei Cento Cavalli calibration cases; it reads as a locally notable, officially designated specimen rather than a destination in its own right. Second, and separately disqualifying on its own until resolved: the writer who verified it could not confirm public access on the ground, 'no source this pass confirmed a specific public path or explicit right of access', which hard rule 10 requires before a page sends anyone there. Keep this lead if either changes: real evidence of outside interest (press, listicles, search demand), or a confirmed public path/access point (the Ypres OSM-footpath technique in BRIEF_RESEARCH.md, or a direct check with Camara Municipal de Lagos). The full written story sits in git history (data/research/lagos-pt-verified.json as of 2026-09-12, since cleared) so a future pass does not have to re-verify from zero if it clears either bar.
leads.source: data/registers/portugal-icnf.json entry KNJ1/573 (ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico, CC BY 4.0); https://algarvevivo.pt/arvores-monumentais-no-algarve/

leads.name: No further register or named candidates found in Lagos town itself
leads.reason: This pass searched Lagos's historic parks and gardens (Jardim da Constituicao, Praca Gil Eanes and the old town/castle walls), churches, the ICNF national register (only one entry in the whole concelho: lgp_001), a regional roundup of Algarve monumental trees (algarvevivo.pt), a 'greatest trees of Portugal' listicle (none in the Algarve west of Sao Bras de Alportel, 80km+ away), a local news search on Lagos's own tree-classification process, and a nearby natural-springs park (Sitio das Fontes, which turned out to be in neighbouring Lagoa municipality, not Lagos, and does not name individual trees anyway). A November 2019 Lagos Municipal Assembly motion asked the council to survey the whole municipality for classification-worthy trees; no evidence was found that this survey produced a published list, so Lagos may simply be a 'nobody has named its trees' city per the pattern in BRIEF_RESEARCH.md. Next pass should try: the parish churches by name (Igreja de Santo Antonio, Igreja de Sao Sebastiao, Igreja Santa Maria), Ponta da Piedade cliff walks, and a direct query/email-style check of the Camara Municipal de Lagos rather than press coverage.
leads.source: n/a (negative result recorded from this pass's own searches)
